description: Remove the GitHub personal access token from the client bundle. The token is currently read as import.meta.env.VITE_GITHUB_KEY in src/components/GithubContributions.jsx and sent as an Authorization header. Because the VITE_ prefix makes Vite inline the value at build time, the token ships in plaintext to every visitor. Replace the runtime authenticated request with a build-time fetch that writes a static JSON file, so no credential ever reaches the browser.
notes: Code work complete and verified 2026-08-12. .env renamed VITE_GITHUB_KEY -> GITHUB_TOKEN; .env.example added; scripts/fetch-github.mjs added and wired into the build script (node --env-file-if-exists=.env scripts/fetch-github.mjs && vite build); GithubContributions.jsx now fetches /github-contributions.json with no auth header; axios removed from package.json and yarn.lock. Verified: yarn lint passes, yarn build passes, `grep -rl 'ghp_' dist/` = 0, the literal token value appears 0 times in dist/, `grep -r 'VITE_GITHUB_KEY' src/ scripts/` = 0, no import.meta.env left in src/, and the preview server returns the JSON at 200 application/json. public/github-contributions.json is committed as a fallback so the section still renders if a build runs without the token. TWO HUMAN ACTIONS REMAIN AND ARE NOT DONE: (1) add GITHUB_TOKEN to the Vercel project environment variables via the dashboard, and (2) revoke the old leaked token at https://github.com/settings/tokens — it is still live and is present in the previously deployed bundle, so it must be treated as compromised.

description: Fix the project card aria-label that hides all card content from screen readers. In src/components/Projects.jsx an <a> wraps the entire card and carries aria-label="View details about the project {title}". Because aria-label on a link overrides its subtree's accessible name, screen reader users hear only that label and lose the h3, the description paragraph, and every technology chip. The label is also factually wrong: the href points to the live external site, not a details page.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the vite dev server on localhost:3000. Took PRD step 1's aria-labelledby option rather than deleting the label outright: the <a> wraps the ENTIRE card, so with no label at all the computed name becomes the whole subtree concatenated ('Screenshot of the project X X <150-word description> TypeScript Node.js ... View Project') — technically compliant but a worse announcement. Each card now has aria-labelledby={`project-title-N project-new-tab-N`}, pointing at the existing h3 (now id'd) and a new sr-only span '(opens in a new tab)' placed beside the visible 'View Project' CTA. The new-tab hint lives in its own span rather than inside the h3 so the heading's own accessible name stays exactly the project title in the heading rotor. VERIFIED IN CHROME'S REAL A11Y TREE (not just my own accname replication): the three links compute to 'Dualmint Marketplace (opens in a new tab)', 'Ipseity Network (opens in a new tab)', 'Real-Time Collaborative Editor (opens in a new tab)'; Playwright's own getByRole resolution independently reported the same three names. Description paragraphs and all 15 technology chips remain as separate nodes in the a11y tree under each link, none inside an aria-hidden subtree; 0 duplicate ids and 0 dangling idref on the page; target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer intact on all 3 cards plus the 'All Projects' link. No visual change: the sr-only span computes to position absolute / 1x1 / clip rect(0,0,0,0) on all 3 cards, screenshots show the CTA row unchanged, no horizontal overflow at 780px or 375px, hover still applies rgba(147,51,234,0.6) to the card border, and the link is still focusable and focus lands on it. yarn lint passes, yarn build passes, and the old label string appears 0 times in src/ AND 0 times in the built bundle. CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM'S PREMISE, worth knowing for A11Y-005/006: the claim that screen reader users 'lose the h3, the description paragraph, and every technology chip' was overstated for the raw a11y tree — a BEFORE snapshot showed Chrome still exposed the h3, paragraph and chips as descendants even with the aria-label present. What was genuinely broken is the announced accessible NAME (wrong text, and the only thing many SRs read when the link is focused or listed in the links rotor), and that it falsely promised a details page. The fix is still correct; the severity framing was just sharper than the tree warranted.

description: Fix the five WCAG AA color contrast failures. text-neutral-500 (#737373) on the bg-neutral-950 (#0a0a0a) page background measures 4.18:1, and 3.78:1 where it sits on bg-neutral-900 cards. Both fall short of the 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text. Changing to text-neutral-400 (#a3a3a3) yields 7.85:1 and passes comfortably with a barely perceptible visual change.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the vite dev server on localhost:3000. All five text locations moved to text-neutral-400; `grep -rc text-neutral-500 src/` totals exactly 1 (the 36px 'Me' in About.jsx, deliberately kept per step 2). border-neutral-800 -> border-neutral-700 in Hero/About/Technologies(x2)/Projects, leaving 0 occurrences of border-neutral-800; email underline purple-400/40 -> /70. All five borders confirmed rgb(64,64,64) and the underline rgba(192,132,252,0.7) in the browser. AXE RESULT: 0 color-contrast violations, 86 passes. >>> BUT STEP 6 HAD TO BE RUN WITH A TEST-ONLY WORKAROUND, READ THIS <<< Run straight, axe reports 86 color-contrast VIOLATIONS that are all false positives: it resolves the page background to #ffffff and reports the light text as failing against white. Cause: html and body are both rgba(0,0,0,0) and the dark ground is painted only by the fixed z-[-1] div in src/App.jsx:13, which a contrast algorithm cannot attribute as an element's background. That is exactly the defect POLISH-001 step 2 owns. To get a real measurement I set document.body.style.backgroundColor='#0a0a0a' at test time only (source untouched); axe then returned 0 violations / 86 passes. ONCE POLISH-001 LANDS, AXE WILL PASS NATIVELY AND THIS WORKAROUND CAN BE DROPPED — until then any axe run on this page reports garbage contrast numbers, so do not trust a raw axe scan here. A further 30 nodes come back 'incomplete' (background gradient) covering Hero, About and the Technologies heading, including the four About dt labels this item changed, so axe could not confirm those. Verified them empirically instead: hid all content except the painter div, screenshotted, and scanned every pixel for the brightest background on the page — rgb(35,35,53) at the top centre. Against that true worst case, neutral-400 measures 6.11:1 on the page and 6.54:1 on the card fill (both need 4.5), neutral-300 body copy 10.39:1, and purple-400 links 5.83:1. The OLD neutral-500 measures 3.25:1 there, so the defect was real and somewhat worse than this item's flat-background estimate of 4.18:1. The kept 'Me' at 36px needs only 3:1 and measures 3.25:1 — it passes, but the margin is thinner than the 4.18 figure implied, so do not reuse neutral-500 for anything smaller. >>> STEP 4 DOES NOT ACHIEVE WHAT IT CLAIMS — IMPLEMENTED AS SPECIFIED, BUT THE PREMISE IS WRONG <<< border-neutral-700 measures 1.91:1 against #0a0a0a and 1.49:1 at the gradient peak, NOT the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 requires; the step's own reasoning does not hold. (border-neutral-800 was 1.31:1, so this is still a real ~46% improvement in delineation, just not a conformance fix.) Reaching 3:1 needs about neutral-500 (4.18:1 flat / 3.25:1 at peak) — neutral-600 only reaches 2.53:1 — which is a much more visible design change than 'barely perceptible', so it is the user's call and was NOT taken unilaterally. Also worth knowing: the cards are not delineated by the border alone as the step assumes; they carry bg-neutral-900/40, though that fill is only 1.03:1 against the page so it contributes almost nothing. Whether 1.4.11 even applies is arguable, since these are decorative borders around static content rather than UI component boundaries. STEP 7 CANNOT BE DONE FROM HERE: WAVE runs against a deployed URL and these changes are not deployed. Also confirmed: no horizontal overflow at 375px, all 30 reveals still reach opacity 1, the GithubContributions error state was exercised for real (by temporarily moving public/github-contributions.json aside, then restored byte-identical) and renders at rgb(163,163,163); the loading state shares an identical class string and is covered by the same edit but was not separately forced. yarn lint and yarn build both pass.

description: Optimize the image payload, which is the single largest performance problem in the repo: roughly 4.5MB of images are shipped to render three 200px-wide thumbnails and one 384px avatar. Two files are PNG data misnamed with a .jpg extension (project-1.jpg is 2.2MB at 1900x1318; project-3.jpg is 2245x1324), dilsherSinghProfile.png is a 1.2MB photo stored as PNG at 1024x1024, and project-2.png is 922KB at 2553x1308. Vite copies all of them into dist byte-for-byte with zero optimization.
notes: Complete and verified 2026-08-12. dist/assets went 4.5MB -> 288KB; the four images total 78KB, down from 4.4MB. STRUCTURE: full-resolution sources moved to src/assets/originals/ with extensions corrected to match their real encoding (project-1.jpg and project-3.jpg were PNG data — confirmed by magic bytes — and are now project-1.png / project-3.png). Nothing imports src/assets/originals/, so Vite never bundles it; it is the pipeline's input only. Generated WebP lives in src/assets/optimized/ and IS committed, so a build still succeeds on a host where sharp's platform binary is unusable. src/assets/projects/ no longer exists. Deleted the unreferenced src/assets/dilsherSinghProfile.jpg (174KB). PIPELINE: scripts/optimize-images.mjs (new) uses sharp 0.35.3 (added as a devDependency via yarn, so yarn.lock stays in yarn-v1 format) and is wired into the build as `node scripts/optimize-images.mjs && node --env-file-if-exists=.env scripts/fetch-github.mjs && vite build`; also exposed as `yarn optimize:images`. Widths are ~2x display size: profile 1024x1024 -> 768x768 (57.8KB), projects -> 400px wide (9.9KB / 5.7KB / 4.2KB). Re-encode is skipped via a sha256 of the source bytes plus the encode settings, recorded in src/assets/optimized/.manifest.json — content-hashed rather than mtime-based because a git checkout does not preserve mtimes. VERIFIED: yarn lint passes; yarn build passes; `du -sk dist/assets` = 288 (target <500); `find dist/assets -type f \( -name '*.webp' -o -name '*.png' -o -name '*.jpg' \) -size +150k | wc -l` = 0; re-running the script is a no-op ('4 images already up to date'); both degradation paths were exercised by hiding node_modules/sharp — outputs present gives a warning and exit 0, an output missing gives a clear error and exit 1. IMAGE 404 CHECK: Playwright could not run in this sandbox (missing browser system libraries), so instead every image URL referenced by the built bundle was extracted from dist/assets/*.js and curled against the vite preview on :3000 — all 4 returned 200 with content-type image/webp, and the only other image (the 1.9KB navbar logo) is inlined as a base64 data URI by Vite so it cannot 404. VISUAL QUALITY: each optimized file was decoded and composited side by side against its original downscaled to true display size (384px / 200px) and inspected — indistinguishable; PSNR at display size is 36.6dB (profile), 32.0dB and 38.0dB for the project shots. NOT DONE HERE ON PURPOSE: width/height attributes on the Projects.jsx and Navbar.jsx images are PERF-002's step 3, and the navbar logo was left alone (2KB, already inlined, and outside this item's four images).

description: Stop delaying the largest contentful paint with entry animations. In src/components/Hero.jsx the LCP image is held at opacity 0 with a 1.2 second animation delay and the bio paragraph is delayed 1 second. This deliberately defers the LCP element by over a second and by itself caps the Lighthouse performance score regardless of any other optimization.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against `vite preview` on localhost:3000 (the BUILT bundle, per steps 4-7), measured before/after with a git worktree of HEAD served on :3001. HEADLINE RESULT: real observed LCP went 2356/2362/2314ms -> 368/156/137ms across three matched Lighthouse runs, and LCP now equals FCP exactly in every run, i.e. the largest paint IS the first paint. THE HERO IMAGE IS NO LONGER WRAPPED IN A Reveal AT ALL — that is the core of the fix and a deliberate deviation from a literal reading of step 1, which only asked to reduce its delay. Any opacity animation on the LCP element defers it regardless of delay, because Chrome does not record an opacity-transitioning element as painted until the transition ENDS (measured: each element's LCP entry lands at FCP + its own delay + its own duration). Rendering the image plainly makes it paint on the first frame independent of hydration; it now carries fetchPriority="high" alongside the existing width/height/loading=eager. Verified by sampling computed opacity every frame from an addInitScript BEFORE navigation: the image exists at 122ms and is opacity 1 on the very first frame it exists, 0 of 67 samples below 1. The four above-the-fold hero TEXT reveals keep their animation but were cut from delays 0/0.5/0.75/1.0 at 0.5s duration to delays 0/0.05/0.1/0.15 at a shared HERO_DURATION of 0.3s, since on narrow viewports the avatar drops below the fold and the h1/bio become the LCP candidates (measured at 375px: LCP 904ms -> 592ms). Whole hero now settles in 0.45s vs 1.7s. Below-the-fold reveals were left at the 0.5s default. STEP 3: width/height added to all 3 Projects.jsx images and the Navbar logo (562x106); all 5 images on the page now have both attributes and every attribute ratio matches its natural ratio exactly. The project dimensions are NOT hardcoded — scripts/optimize-images.mjs now emits src/assets/optimized/dimensions.json (committed, imported by src/constants/index.js as project.imageSize) so a change to the pipeline's target width can never leave a stale aspect ratio in the markup; the manifest values became {key,width,height} to carry them, which re-encoded all four images once to byte-IDENTICAL output. HONEST CAVEAT ON CLS: 0 before and 0 after, with zero layout-shift entries even scrolling the full page at 400kbps. The width/height attributes do demonstrably reserve the box (the project images report complete:false with their final height already correct), but I could not produce a measurable shift in the baseline to fix — Chrome's lazy-load threshold fetches those images well before they enter the viewport, and off-screen shifts do not count toward CLS. Step 3 is correct defensive practice, not a measured win. STEP 7 CAVEAT WORTH READING: Lighthouse mobile scored 99/99/99 (median 99, target 95) — but the BASELINE also scored 99/99/99 with the same simulated LCP of 2.1s. Lighthouse's simulated (Lantern) throttling models network and CPU critical paths and is BLIND to CSS transition wall-clock time, so it did not detect this defect at all; only the observed metric did. Do not use the simulated Lighthouse score to validate animation-related LCP work. Also confirmed: RENDER-001's guarantees still hold (reducedMotion 'reduce' -> all 30 reveals at opacity 1 / transform none, hero image opacity 1), the entry animation still visibly plays for normal visitors (partial opacity and offset both observed on the h1, settling at opacity 1 / transform none), reveal count 31 -> 30 confirming exactly one Reveal removed, yarn lint passes, yarn build passes, and the only console error is the pre-existing sandbox-firewall cert failure on fonts.googleapis.com. NOT DONE, OWNED ELSEWHERE: Lighthouse still flags render-blocking-resources (~450ms) and prioritize-lcp-image (~300ms, wants a preload hint) — both are the Google Fonts @import and head-resource work that PERF-003 and SEO-003 own; uses-responsive-images wants a srcset, which no PRD item currently covers.

description: Fix the render-blocking font load and add caching headers. The Inter font is pulled in via a CSS @import at the top of src/index.css, which is the slowest possible path: the browser must download and parse index.css before it even discovers the font CSS URL, then fetch that, then the font files. The request also asks for the full 100-900 weight range in both roman and italic, but the site uses no italics. Separately there is no vercel.json, so hash-named immutable assets are served with max-age=0.
steps: Move the Google Fonts request from the @import in src/index.css to <link> tags in index.html, paired with the preconnect hints from SEO-003, keeping display=swap which is already present.
Drop the unused italic axis from the font URL, keeping only the roman weights the site actually uses.
Assert the import is gone: `grep -c '@import url("https://fonts' src/index.css` must output 0.
Create vercel.json setting 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable' for /assets/* (safe because Vite hash-names these files) and 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' for HTML.
Add the security headers X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and X-Frame-Options DENY in the same vercel.json.
Validate the config parses: `node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("vercel.json","utf8"))'`.
After deploying, assert `curl -sI https://www.dilshersingh.com/assets/<hashed-file>.js | grep -i cache-control` reports max-age=31536000 and immutable.
After deploying, assert the HTML response still reports must-revalidate so users get new deploys immediately.
Confirm in Lighthouse that 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' no longer flags the font stylesheet.

description: Split the JavaScript bundle. The production build emits a single 335KB chunk (112KB gzipped) containing React, framer-motion, and react-icons alongside all application code, so any source change invalidates the entire cached bundle for returning visitors.
steps: Add build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks to vite.config.js separating react/react-dom, framer-motion, and react-icons into distinct vendor chunks.
Run `yarn build` and confirm dist/assets contains more than one .js file.
Assert no single JS chunk exceeds 150KB raw.
Confirm total gzipped JS does not increase relative to the current 112KB baseline (splitting should not add meaningful overhead).
Confirm the site still renders and the contributions graph still loads after splitting.

description: Make entry animations degrade to visible content, and honor prefers-reduced-motion. This is a hard prerequisite for RENDER-002: every whileInView animation sets initial={{ opacity: 0 }} as an inline style, so prerendering the app as-is would emit HTML whose text is present but invisible, which search engines may discount and which would defeat the purpose of prerendering. Additionally none of the 7 animating components honors prefers-reduced-motion; because framer-motion writes inline styles, a CSS media query cannot override it and the fix must happen in JS.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12. All 31 entry animations across Hero, About, Technologies, Experience, Projects, GithubContributions and Contact were converted from framer-motion to a new src/components/Reveal.jsx (IntersectionObserver + CSS classes) plus a `.reveal` block in src/index.css. The base state is now VISIBLE: hiding only applies under `.js .reveal` inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), and the `js` class is added by a synchronous inline script in index.html <head>. So content is visible for crawlers, for JS-off visitors, and under reduced motion, and there is no visible-then-hidden flash once RENDER-002 prerenders. DEVIATION FROM STEP 1: <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"> was deliberately NOT added. Converting every animation left zero framer-motion imports in src/, so MotionConfig would have had nothing to configure. Reduced motion is instead handled by the CSS media query, which is strictly stronger — it applies before hydration and with JS disabled, neither of which MotionConfig can do. framer-motion is still listed in package.json but is now unused; removing it was left out of scope (note PERF-004 references it as a vendor chunk). Side effect: main JS chunk 299KB -> 187KB (gzip 100KB -> 63.5KB). Browser-verified on the built preview at localhost:3000 with Playwright: reducedMotion 'reduce' -> all 31 reveals at opacity 1 / transform none immediately and before any is-visible class is applied; default motion -> below-fold elements correctly staged at opacity 0 translateY(-40px) then transition in on scroll, and a full viewport-by-viewport scroll pass revealed 31/31 with 0 stranded; javaScriptEnabled:false against a prerender stand-in (client DOM baked into dist/index.html with the module script stripped) -> all 7 headings visible, hero bio visible, 0 of 31 reveals hidden, and 0 occurrences of inline 'opacity:0' in that 107KB static HTML, which pre-validates RENDER-002's final assertion; 0 console errors/warnings; no horizontal overflow at 375px despite the translateX offsets. Step 7's dist/index.html grep still cannot be run for real until RENDER-002 lands. UPDATE 2026-08-12, RENDER-002 has now landed and step 7 was run for real against the prerendered dist/index.html: `grep -o 'opacity:0' dist/index.html | wc -l` outputs 0, and a JS-disabled load of the genuinely prerendered page shows all 7 headings at opacity 1 with 0 of 30 reveals hidden. This item's design held up under prerendering with no changes, including no flash of visible-then-hidden content.
steps: Wrap the app tree in <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"> in src/App.jsx, which makes all framer-motion animations respect the OS-level reduced-motion setting globally.

Convert entry animations so the base rendered state is visible and the animation is additive, replacing inline initial opacity 0 with a CSS keyframe or IntersectionObserver-applied class across the roughly 20 animated elements in About, Technologies, Experience, Projects, GithubContributions, and Contact.
Keep the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block in src/index.css that resets scroll-behavior, which is already correct.
Playwright with reduced motion: newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }), load the page, and assert every section's text is visible with computed opacity 1 immediately, with no transform offset.
Playwright with default motion: assert the entry animations still play for normal visitors, so the visual design is preserved.
Playwright: disable JavaScript, load the built preview, and assert section text is still visible with opacity 1 (this is what validates the prerender path).
Assert no inline opacity:0 remains in the built HTML: after RENDER-002 lands, `grep -o 'opacity:0' dist/index.html | wc -l` must output 0.

description:
Prerender the single route to static HTML so crawlers and link-preview bots receive real content. The deployed page is currently a 1212-byte empty shell containing only
, so search engines and social scrapers see no content. Use native Vite SSG (vite build --ssr plus renderToString) rather than Vike or a migration to Astro or Next: the site has exactly one route and no router, so SSG costs about 30 lines of config and zero component rewrites, whereas a framework migration would mean rewriting all 8 components for no additional SEO benefit. Note that vite-plugin-ssr has been renamed Vike, so that package name is outdated. Depends on RENDER-001.
notes:
Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against `vite preview` on localhost:3000 (the BUILT bundle). dist/index.html went from a 3,997-byte shell to 60,454 bytes; prerender injects 56,437 characters. Note the item's '1212 bytes' figure is stale — the shell had already grown to 3,997 bytes when SEO-001 and the redesign added the meta/JSON-LD block; the defect itself (empty
) was exactly as described. Zero component rewrites were needed: every component was already SSR-safe, since the only browser globals in src/ were document.getElementById in main.jsx and Reveal.jsx's IntersectionObserver, which is inside useEffect and additionally guarded by a typeof check. FILES: src/entry-server.jsx (new, exports render() = renderToString of the same StrictMode+App tree as main.jsx); src/main.jsx createRoot -> hydrateRoot; scripts/prerender.mjs (new); build chain is now optimize-images && fetch-github && vite build && vite build --ssr src/entry-server.jsx --outDir dist/server && node scripts/prerender.mjs. THE BIGGEST RISK WAS ASSET-HASH DRIFT AND IT DID NOT MATERIALIZE: the SSR build resolves image imports to the same content-hashed /assets/ URLs as the client build, verified by extracting all 6 asset URLs from the prerendered HTML and confirming each resolves to a real file in dist/. If that ever drifts, the prerendered tags would 404 silently — check it first if images vanish. TWO DELIBERATE ADDITIONS BEYOND THE STEPS: (1) prerender.mjs deletes dist/server after injecting, because dist/ is what Vercel deploys and leaving it there would publish a second full copy of the app bundle; (2) unlike fetch-github.mjs and optimize-images.mjs, which degrade gracefully, prerender.mjs FAILS THE BUILD on any problem (missing template, missing root div, render() returning under 1000 chars) — there is no fallback for prerendering, and silently emitting the empty shell would ship the exact defect this item exists to fix. HYDRATION WAS VERIFIED BY NODE IDENTITY, NOT JUST BY AN EMPTY CONSOLE: a production React build strips most dev warnings, so 'no console errors' is weak evidence here. Instead an addInitScript MutationObserver captured a reference to the prerendered

the instant the parser created it; after hydration that captured node is === the live h1, still isConnected, and carries a __reactFiber key. React therefore attached to the server markup rather than discarding it. (A first attempt at this observed document.documentElement, which is null at document_start, so the observer never installed and reported a meaningless 0 mutations — observe `document` instead.) Exactly one node is removed during hydration, a

, which is the GithubContributions loading paragraph swapping to the ready state; that is step 6 working as designed, confirmed by dist/index.html containing 'Loading contribution activity' once and 'contributions in the last year' zero times. STEP 10 (JS disabled): all 7 headings — h1 'Dilsher Singh' plus About Me / Technologies / Experience / Projects / GitHub Contributions / Get in Touch — render at computed opacity 1, html.className is empty (the inline js-class script never runs), and 0 of 30 .reveal elements are hidden. STEP 11: 0 hydration errors; the only console error is the pre-existing fonts.googleapis.com cert failure from the sandbox firewall. STEP 12: clicking the Projects nav link scrolls 0 -> 3263px, and the heatmap populates post-hydration with 368 cells and '1,582 contributions in the last year'. NO FLASH OF UNSTYLED/UNHIDDEN CONTENT, which was the main visual risk once #root stopped being empty: sampling the h1's computed opacity every frame from document_start shows it at 0 on the very first frame it exists (119ms) and rising monotonically to 1, with no 1-then-lower transition anywhere. RENDER-001's inline head script holds up exactly as it was designed to. PERF-002 NOT REGRESSED: LCP 156/180/112ms across 3 runs, each equal to FCP with the hero IMG as the LCP element, CLS 0 — if anything better than PERF-002's 368/156/137, since the image now ships in the initial HTML instead of being injected by JS. RENDER-001's step 7 can now be run for real and passes: `grep -o 'opacity:0' dist/index.html | wc -l` outputs 0. Also confirmed: no secrets in the prerendered HTML (0 hits for ghp_/github_token/authorization), 30 reveals with 0 stranded after a full scroll pass, yarn lint passes, yarn build passes. EXPECTED BUILD WARNING, DO NOT 'FIX' IT: the prerender prints 'React does not recognize the fetchPriority prop'. React DOM 18's SERVER renderer lacks fetchPriority in its known-prop list while the client renderer has it; it still emits the attribute, and HTML attribute names are case-insensitive, so the browser sees fetchpriority="high" and the preload hint is intact (verified in dist/index.html). Lowercasing the JSX silences the warning but trades it for a react/no-unknown-property LINT ERROR, so the camelCase spelling stays; React 19 resolves it. A comment in Hero.jsx records this. STEP 13 CANNOT BE DONE FROM HERE — it needs a deploy: after deploying, `curl -s https://www.dilshersingh.com | grep -c 'Senior full stack'` must return at least 1.
steps: Confirm RENDER-001 is complete first; prerendering before it would bake opacity:0 into the static HTML.

Confirm interactive behavior still works post-hydration: nav anchor links scroll, and the contributions graph populates.
After deploying, confirm `curl -s https://www.dilshersingh.com | grep -c 'Senior full stack'` returns at least 1.

description: Harden the toolchain. The ralph.sh automation loop invokes `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test`, but neither script exists in package.json and no test framework is installed, so those feedback loops cannot currently pass. There is also no accessibility linting, no pinned Node version, the react-hooks ESLint plugin sits on a release candidate, and README.md is still unmodified create-vite boilerplate.
steps: Decide and implement how the loop's feedback gates resolve: either add real typecheck and test scripts (Vitest plus Playwright, which also enables every browserTest item in this PRD), or update ralph.sh and ralph-once.sh to invoke `yarn lint` and `yarn build`, which do exist. Do not leave the loop referencing scripts that are absent.
Add eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y and enable its recommended rules so the accessibility fixes in this PRD cannot silently regress.
Re-enable the react/jsx-no-target-blank rule currently disabled in eslint.config.js; the code already complies, so this only restores the guardrail.
Move eslint-plugin-react-hooks off the 5.1.0-rc.0 release candidate onto a stable release.
Add .nvmrc and an engines field pinning Node 22 to match the local toolchain, since nothing currently constrains the build host's Node version.
Replace the boilerplate README.md with real documentation: what the project is, how to run it, the required GITHUB_TOKEN env var, and the prerender build pipeline.

Assert every script the automation references actually exists: for each of typecheck and test, `node -e "process.exit(require('./package.json').scripts.typecheck ? 0 : 1)"` must exit 0, or confirm the shell scripts no longer reference them.

description: Produce a written content review as a deliverable only. Per explicit instruction, propose rewrites but do not modify any copy. Write docs/content-review.md with before and after rewrites for each finding below, and wait for approval before any wording changes.
